title: Finite-cover exact sequence for a local system on the complement of a divisor
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient ring $A=A_{E,n}$ and algebraically closed field $k$ of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], and use sheaves of $A$-modules on small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Let $X$ be a normal separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], where normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain. Let $f\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ and let $i:Z=V(f)\hookrightarrow X$ be an effective principal Cartier divisor, meaning that $f$ is a non-zero-divisor in every local ring [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Put $U=X\setminus Z$ and let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be the open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. For a generic point $\xi$ of a component of $Z$, every constructible etale sheaf $F$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] on $X$ with $i^*F=0$ becomes $j_!G$ for a finite locally constant sheaf $G$ on $U$ after replacing $X$ by an open neighbourhood of $\xi$ (and restricting $Z,U,i,j,F$).

For any finite locally constant $G$ on $U$, there is a finite etale surjection $p:U'\to U$ trivializing $G$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Let $q:X'\to X$ be the normalization extending $p$: on each component of $X$ it is the disjoint union of the relative spectra of the integral closures of $\mathcal O_X$ in the function fields of the components of $U'$. Then $q$ is finite, $X'$ is normal, $Z'=q^{-1}Z$ is an effective principal Cartier divisor, and $U'=X'\setminus Z'$. With $j':U'\hookrightarrow X'$ and $G'=\operatorname{coker}(G\to p_*p^*G)$, the sheaf $G'$ is finite locally constant and there is a short exact sequence
$$0\longrightarrow j_!G\longrightarrow q_*j'_!p^*G\longrightarrow j_!G'\longrightarrow0.$$
Moreover $Rq_*j'_!p^*G=q_*j'_!p^*G$ and $q^*j_!G=j'_!p^*G$. Geometric stalks of $q_*$ are finite products of the stalks over the given geometric point; $q_*$ is exact on etale $A$-module sheaves. Each point of $Z'$ over a generic point of a component of $Z$ is generic in a component of $Z'$.

Here normalization is [def-fin-normalization-extension], extension by zero is [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero], ordinary direct image is [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], and inverse image is [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]; derived functors are taken in the derived categories of [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories].

source.place: Claim 3.2.3 proof, second paragraph: finite coefficient sheaf, finite etale trivialization, normalization, and induction on k

proof.text: First record the local geometry used below. Finite type over the field makes $X$ Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] (a field is Noetherian since its only ideals are $0$ and itself). On any affine open $T$, [lem-sbc-normal-sections-finite-product] writes $\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_X)$ as a finite product of integrally closed domains. The spectra of the factors are disjoint open-and-closed integral normal pieces: a prime of a finite product contains all but one factor idempotent. Thus the irreducible components of $X$ are locally open and disjoint, hence globally open and closed; quasi-compactness makes their number finite. We can work componentwise, and near the chosen $\xi$ we can work on an integral affine neighbourhood. Empty $X$ and empty $Z$ have no generic point to check.

source.place: Claim 3.2.3, first sentence; local geometry expanded using Stacks Tags 01T6 and 0357

proof.text: On the integral component through $\xi$, the non-zero-divisor $f$ is nonzero and vanishes at $\xi$. Therefore $\xi$ is not the generic point $\eta$ of $X$, and its local dimension is positive by [lem-sc-scheme-stalk-dimension-generalization-chains]. Apply [lem-sbc-locally-principal-support-dimension-one] to the principal ideal $(f)$ at $\xi$. It produces a generalization $\xi'$ in $V(f)$ with local dimension one. Since $\xi$ is generic in a component of $V(f)$, any such generalization in $V(f)$ equals $\xi$. Hence $\dim\mathcal O_{X,\xi}=1$. The chain formula now says that the only strict generalization of $\xi$ is $\eta$.

source.place: Claim 3.2.3, shrinking about the generic point; Stacks Tag 0BJG

proof.text: Apply [prop-constructible-generic-constancy] to the constructible module sheaf $F$ to obtain a dense open $V\subseteq X$ where $F$ is finite locally constant. Use the module category throughout; its constructibility is precisely the finite lisse stratification in [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. Put $B=X\setminus V$. By [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components], the closed subset $B\cap U$ of the Noetherian open $U$ has finitely many irreducible components with generic points $b_1,\ldots,b_s$. None is $\eta$, because $V$ is dense. Its closure in $X$ is the union of the $\overline{\{b_a\}}$. If this union contained $\xi$, some $b_a\in U$ would strictly generalize $\xi$ and differ from $\eta$, contrary to Step 2. Remove that union, retaining an open neighbourhood of $\xi$. On its complement of $Z$, $G=j^*F$ is now finite locally constant. The localization triangle [lem-cbc-open-closed-recollement] has third term $i_*i^*F=0$, so its counit identifies $F$ with $j_!G$. All these restrictions retain $\xi$.

source.place: Claim 3.2.3, general case: replacing X by an open subset containing the generic point

proof.text: Now take any finite locally constant $G$ on $U$, independently of the preceding shrinking. By [fin2-lem-lisse-trivialized-finite-etale], choose a finite etale surjection $p:U'\to U$ for which $p^*G$ is constant with finite module fibre on each connected component. This is the componentwise meaning of trivialization when $U$ is disconnected. Thus $p^*G$ is finite locally constant, and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-finite-pushforward-locally-constant] makes $H=p_*p^*G$ finite locally constant. Since the finite ring $A$ is Noetherian (every ascending chain of its finitely many ideals stabilizes), [lem-weil-pbc-locally-constant-derived-serre] implies that $G'=\operatorname{coker}(G\to H)$ is locally constant of finite type. A module generated by $r$ elements over finite $A$ is a quotient of the finite set $A^r$, so $G'$ is finite locally constant in the finite-stalk sense as well.

source.place: Claim 3.2.3, finite etale covering and local-system cokernel; Stacks Tags 095B and 093U

proof.text: The natural map $G\to H$ is the unit for $p^*\dashv p_*$. At a geometric point $\bar u$, the restriction-of-germs formula [lem-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula-restriction] identifies $H_{\bar u}$ with the product of $(p^*G)_{\bar u'}$ over the finite geometric fibre. Under [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ], the component of the unit at each $\bar u'$ sends a germ $a$ to that same germ $a$. The unit is therefore the diagonal $G_{\bar u}\to\prod_{\bar u'}G_{\bar u}$, which is injective because $p$ is surjective and the fibre is nonempty. Exactness of geometric stalks [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] gives zero stalks for its kernel, and [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] makes that kernel zero. Thus $0\to G\to H\to G'\to0$ is short exact. These stalk maps are $A$-linear: germ restriction and pullback commute with multiplication by every scalar, so the abelian-group stalk statements apply to the same module sheaves.

source.place: Claim 3.2.3, natural embedding; Stacks Tags 03QP and 03Q1 with the unit map identified

proof.text: Construct $X'$ componentwise as stated. Each component of normal $X$ is integral by Step 1, and its open $U$ is nonempty and normal because a non-zero-divisor cannot vanish at its generic point. The source $U'$ is Noetherian (finite over the finite-type $U$); [lem-fin-etale-normal-components] splits its restriction over each such component into finitely many normal integral open-and-closed pieces $P$. Each $P\to U$ is connected finite etale, with a finite extension $k(P)/k(X)$. Use [def-fin-normalization-extension] to form the normalization in this extension. It is finite by [lem-fin-normalization-extension-finite], and [lem-fin-normalization-extends-cover] identifies its restriction to $U$ with $P$. Taking their finite disjoint union gives precisely the stated $q$, which is finite and satisfies $q^{-1}U=U'$. On an affine chart the integral closure of its coordinate domain in $k(P)$ has integrally closed domain localizations by [lem-sbc-integral-closure-finite-normal-product], applied to the singleton product consisting of the field $k(P)$. Thus all local rings of $X'$ are integrally closed domains.

source.place: Claim 3.2.3, normalization extending the finite etale cover; Stacks Tags 035H, 035L and 033C

proof.text: On such an affine normalization chart $B\subseteq k(P)$ over $R\subseteq k(X)$, the image of $f$ is nonzero, because $R\to k(P)$ is injective and $f$ is nonzero on the component. Since $B$ is a domain, multiplication by $f$ is injective, also after localization. Consequently $Z'=q^{-1}Z=V(q^*f)$ is an effective principal Cartier divisor. Its complement is $q^{-1}U=U'$ from Step 6, so the square with $j,j'$ and $q,p$ is cartesian.

source.place: Claim 3.2.3, pullback of the principal divisor under normalization

proof.text: Apply the exact functor $j_!$ of [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact] to the short exact sequence of Step 5. The finite-open comparison [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-extension-zero] for the cartesian square of Step 7 identifies $j_!H=j_!p_*p^*G$ with $q_*j'_!p^*G$. Its maps commute with each scalar action by naturality, so this abelian-sheaf comparison is an isomorphism of $A$-module sheaves. Substituting it yields the stated short exact sequence with first arrow the extension of the unit. The module-sheaf base-change isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-modules], applied to the same square, gives $q^*j_!G\cong j'_!p^*G$.

source.place: Claim 3.2.3, the cokernel after extension by zero; Stacks Tags 03DJ, 0GJ1 and 03S6

proof.text: For any module sheaf $L$ on $X'$, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula-restriction] gives $(q_*L)_{\bar x}=\prod_{q\bar x'=\bar x}L_{\bar x'}$, with finite index set. As in Step 5 these restriction maps are $A$-linear. Finite products of short exact sequences of modules are exact: kernels are componentwise and any tuple in a product of quotients has a tuple of lifts. Apply this to stalks of a short exact sequence and use [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] and [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] to conclude that $q_*$ is exact on $A$-module sheaves. Its positive right derived functors vanish by the exact-direct-image assertion [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact]; equivalently, applying this exact functor to an injective resolution gives a resolution of its ordinary image. Hence $Rq_*j'_!p^*G=q_*j'_!p^*G$. No flatness or freeness of the finite module fibres is used.

source.place: Claim 3.2.3, finite direct image; Stacks Tag 03QP (including all finite module coefficients)

proof.text: Finally let $x'\in Z'$ map to a generic point $\xi$ of a component of $Z$. On an affine chart write $R\to B$ for the finite integral map and $\mathfrak q$ for $x'$, contracting to the prime $\mathfrak p$ of $\xi$, which is minimal over $(f)$. If a prime $\mathfrak r\subseteq\mathfrak q$ of $B$ contains $f$, its contraction contains $f$ and lies in $\mathfrak p$, hence equals $\mathfrak p$ by minimality. Incomparability [pqf-lem-incomparability] then gives $\mathfrak r=\mathfrak q$. Thus $\mathfrak q$ is minimal among primes containing $f$ in $B$, exactly the condition for $x'$ to be generic in a component of $V(f)=Z'$. This argument permits ramification and nonreduced $Z$ and $Z'$.

source.place: Claim 3.2.3, generic vanishing after finite normalization; Stacks Tag 00GT

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q27-af2d96d44 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read all of it: the item, all 10 steps, the statements of all 27 cited nodes (including the blueprint_update statements of the 8 that have one), the parent lem-trf-dnc-generic-zero-section-vanishing and its Step 4, unit sk-i-curve-zero, and the main-20261015 ancestor lem-trf-local-term-locality. Source checked: Varshavsky arXiv math/0505564, §3.2.2 and Claim 3.2.3 (local PDF). The statement is faithful to the general-case paragraph of Claim 3.2.3: shrink so that F=j_!G with G a local system, take a finite etale trivialization and the normalization X'->X, then the cokernel G' and its exact sequence. The source writes f_! for the finite map; the item writes q_*, which is the same functor for a finite map. The item also states what the parent's Step 4 uses: q finite, X' normal, Z' principal Cartier, Rq_*=q_*, q^*j_!G=j'_!p^*G, the finite stalk formula and exactness, and that points of Z' over a generic point of Z are generic in Z'. Nothing is weakened. This is not a target node and no coefficient categories are identified: everything is etale A-module sheaves, with explicit A-linearity remarks where abelian-sheaf lemmas are used. Hypotheses checked step by step. Step 2: 0BJG applies at xi because dim>0 via eta; maximality of xi in V(f) gives local dimension 1, and the chain formula then excludes any intermediate generalization. Step 3: the bad-locus closure misses xi by Step 2, and the recollement triangle has third term 0. Step 5: the unit is the diagonal on stalks by 03QP and 03Q1, and the fibre is nonempty. Step 6: the normal-components, normalization-finite, extends-cover and integral-closure-product lemmas each apply with their hypotheses met. Step 7 is genuinely elementary. Step 8: the finite-open comparison square matches the node's square, and 03S6 is applied with f=q. Step 10: the incomparability argument is correct. Small cases checked: Kummer cover on A^1 with divisor V(t^r), G=0, the identity cover, disconnected U, empty Z, nonreduced divisor. No new nodes; an rg search found no duplicate. I accept all 23 declared tool_uses: each is a generic black box and none replaces a step of the unit's route.
